headline: Decomposing omics into modules, pathway axes, fluxes and cell-state transitions
label: Interpretable Omics Variation Modules
summary: New ICA, tensor, pathway-score and flux-inference methods recast bulk and single-cell omics as interpretable units linked to cancer and aging.
synthesis: The dominant thread is decomposing omics variation into interpretable units rather than individual genes. Robust multi-run ICA yields 105 reproducible iModulons from 778 CHO RNA-seq samples, projectable onto new data. PathwayTheme scores pathways per sample before decomposition and tests components against biological and technical covariates. HOSVD tensor decomposition selects aging-linked genes jointly across mouse hippocampal and colonic transcriptome and methylation data. Metabolic studies shift the unit to sample-specific flux: Recon3D modeling across 33 TCGA types nominates CRLS1, and M-SCAN infers genome-scale fluxes from RNA, mutations and kcat. At single-cell resolution, the units become states and trajectories. A UCE-based framework maps 22,161 bridges among 614 states, Global Tumor Time orders malignant progression in lung adenocarcinoma snRNA-seq from 227 patients, and STAVAG identifies directionally and temporally variable genes in spatial data. The units differ across studies (modules, pathway axes, fluxes, state transitions), and the items do not converge on a shared framework.
